recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. Do not reintroduce detailed websocket protocol prose into core unless FHIR-I decides to move those mechanics back from external Subscription guidance.
issue_request: FHIR-22628 was a Published/Persuasive FHIR-core Subscription change request asking to align websocket subscriptions with REST hooks by allowing notification payloads over the socket instead of documenting only the websocket PING mechanism; it was applied for R5.
initial_application: The Jira application comment cites commits 03a9bc2af6584c50cfe2a38a0545649ee907bdc0 and 70355f13b223012ee7f9f70eb5a999219cfe7fb1. Those commits added websocket notification Bundle workflow text using Subscription.contentType and Subscription.content, and both are contained in the v5.0.0 tag.
additional_context: Subscription remains active in source/fhir.ini. Current source defines Subscription.contentType and Subscription.content generically, lists websocket as a core channel, and points detailed websocket mechanics to the FHIR Subscriptions Backport IG after later R6 cleanup commit e07a4ebf3485b02e47e981f2d2f1488e9d2f1cac moved websocket content to external sources. FHIR-21281 reinforces that id-only payload support applies across all delivery mechanisms.
reconciliation: No source change was made. The current build-scope source no longer has the old PING-only limitation and already conveys that websocket subscriptions can use configured payload content through the general Subscription payload model.

related_jiras.note: Resolved No Change because payload.content=id-only already supports logical-id style websocket notifications across delivery mechanisms.
